motion_keep_agent_route_reason: After a blocked old path, preserve a safe replacement just built for the agent. The old blocked flag otherwise runs frontier fallback in the same tick and discards it. Old seed 934 has 10 such overwrites for A and 5 for B. Default false as requested. Four no-agent tuning controls are byte-identical; the regression test proves the route repair, while live savings remain unmeasured.
motion_sweep_visible_floor_reason: A sweep needs unsearched floor beyond the calibrated bottom camera ray at search_low_m; rotation cannot reveal its blind floor. This filters look eligibility without adding evidence. Default false as requested. Six-house unseen pass, n=1 per house, solid robots, 240 s: total still 152.8 to 139.3 s per pair, room coverage 76.3 to 79.3 percent, confirmed 29/30 both, zero false. House 5021 loses one coverage point and keeps 47 stuck events; 85-90 percent is not achieved.
motion_bounded_inspection_reason: After survivor_dwell_s plus the larger of survivor_lost_s and freshness, end a stationary view on its next failed steady sample. Let a fresh steady dwell finish. Defer the candidate for stuck_blacklist_s without confirming or rejecting it. Old 934 A stood viewing for 22 s. The first timeout lost a valid 5004 dwell, which the revised rule preserves. Default false as requested; all four revised headless controls are byte-identical, and live savings remain unmeasured.
motion_face_visible_reason: An agent arrival may finish facing when its point lies in the central half of both horizontal camera views, or within the existing survivor face tolerance. Offscreen points still need a turn; survivor confirmation keeps its stricter dwell. Default false as requested. Four no-agent controls are byte-identical. The regression test proves in-view arrival; live savings remain unmeasured.
full_snapshot_s_reason: Recover lost radio state at least every ten seconds.
peer_claim_s_reason: Expire claims from disconnected robots after fifteen seconds.
peer_claim_radius_m_reason: A robot claims a 2.5 m circle around the frontier point it is driving to (about one sweep), so its partner picks somewhere else.
grid_size_m_reason: The grid is centred on the entry point, so it must reach the far side of the house from either door.
team_map_planner_reason: Keep the existing planner while the per-source occupancy belief is measured against truth. Enabling this uses the team log-odds layer for occupancy; fresh local free evidence still takes priority over uncertain partner walls. Search ranking is unchanged.
team_map_entry_position_std_m_reason: A nominal launch pad is not an exact physical pose. Start the reported position uncertainty budget at 5 cm, then grow it with travel and yaw uncertainty. This is an engineering prior, not a calibrated covariance.
team_map_entry_yaw_std_deg_reason: Start the nominal pad heading uncertainty budget at 3 degrees. The seed 934 pad mismatch was 2.39 degrees. Grow the budget from IMU noise and bias walk; matching the robot's own map does not make the shared frame exact.
cell_m_reason: Resolve walls and door gaps at 10 cm.
depth_stride_reason: Limit depth projection work to every fourth pixel.
obstacle_min_height_m_reason: Exclude the floor and low depth noise.
obstacle_max_height_m_reason: Ignore ceilings above the robot mast.
free_log_odds_reason: One free ray makes an unknown cell traversable.
occupied_log_odds_reason: A measured hit outweighs a free ray.
log_odds_cap_reason: Allow later depth observations to clear old obstacles.
free_threshold_reason: Require evidence of free space before planning through a cell.
occupied_threshold_reason: One measured hit blocks a cell.
robot_radius_m_reason: Body half-width 0.18 m plus a 7 cm margin. 0.4 m closed the 1.0 m front door and every 0.8 to 0.9 m interior door, so the planner could not enter the house.
body_half_length_m_reason: Half the body's length: Robots/Robot.cs gives the body a CapsuleCollider 0.75 m long along its axis. Forward clearance counts the nose and a turn in place checks both ends (SwingClear); the 0.25 m planning circle alone let robot B's nose hit the foyer-kitchen opening five times on held-out seed 920.
body_track_poses_reason: Poses kept of where this robot's body stood (one per 0.1 m cell of travel, so the last 60 m): a partner's wall reported there is this robot seen by the partner's LiDAR, not the building (one-door seed 922, both robots lost every route at 4 s). 60 m covers a 200 s mission at the measured 0.3 m/s average.
teammate_track_max_m_reason: Between two radio poses of the partner (2 s apart at up to 0.8 m/s plus margin) the straight line it moved along is cleared of this robot's own walls (OccupancyGrid.MarkTeammateFree); longer jumps (contact lost) clear only the new pose, since the path between is unknown.
obstacle_cost_margin_m_reason: Paths pay a cost that rises within 0.6 m beyond the inflated obstacle, so they run down the middle of halls and doorways instead of hugging the inflation edge (the cost map in Kai Nakamura's LiDAR exploration robot).
obstacle_cost_weight_reason: Add a squared clearance cost near obstacles so short routes through jamb edges can lose to wider routes.
stuck_command_mps_reason: Count only sustained forward commands above 15 cm/s, after acceleration.
stuck_measured_mps_reason: Treat forward odometry within 3 cm/s of zero as stalled, including small negative noise.
stuck_window_s_reason: Require 1.2 continuous seconds of commanded travel with negligible measured forward motion.
stuck_strip_depth_m_reason: Mark a 20 cm strip ahead of the body across twice the configured robot radius.
stuck_log_odds_reason: Infer one obstacle hit; three later free depth frames can clear it with the default free update.
stuck_reverse_m_reason: Back up at most 20 cm of estimated travel before turning and replanning.
stuck_reverse_mps_reason: Reverse slowly, clamped to the sensor motion limit.
stuck_reverse_timeout_s_reason: Stop reversing after 2.5 seconds even if reverse odometry also reports no motion.
stuck_turn_deg_reason: Use measured IMU yaw to turn away before retrying a route.
stuck_turn_timeout_s_reason: Bound the turn even if the body cannot rotate.
stuck_repeat_radius_m_reason: Group repeated contacts within 75 cm and exclude frontier goals within that radius of a failed goal.
stuck_repeat_count_reason: Blacklist a goal after three contacts near the same estimated location.
stuck_blacklist_s_reason: Avoid the failed goal area for 30 seconds, then allow a fresh attempt.
ambient_c_reason: Use a neutral prior for cells with no thermal observation.
heat_project_min_c_reason: Project only hot thermal pixels into the heat layer.
fire_c_reason: Treat this temperature and hotter as forbidden.
fire_clearance_m_reason: Keep the requested distance from fire cells.
heat_cost_radius_m_reason: Start increasing path cost before the hard fire margin.
heat_cost_weight_reason: Prefer longer cool paths to paths close to fire.
heat_decay_c_per_s_reason: Keep recently observed fire hot during brief occlusion.
heat_prediction_s_reason: Block cells forecast to cross the fire threshold in the next second.
heat_rise_memory_s_reason: Expire old temperature slopes rather than extrapolate forever.
frame_pair_tolerance_s_reason: Pair thermal and depth only within about one camera period.
frame_max_age_s_reason: Stop driving when geometry, active images, or air samples are stale.
motion_stale_s_reason: Stop integrating a velocity when its sensor stream has stopped.
health_stride_reason: Measure image health on a small grey image.
corner_gradient_reason: Require gradients above sensor noise to count corners.
corner_target_reason: Normalize corner count by forty useful corner patches.
contrast_target_reason: Normalize luminance contrast against a textured scene.
health_threshold_reason: Require more than valid depth alone to trust colour.
health_corner_weight_reason: Give image structure the largest health contribution.
health_contrast_weight_reason: Use luminance variation to detect smoke washout.
health_depth_weight_reason: Include geometry dropout without letting it hide black RGB.
switch_to_thermal_s_reason: Reject short exposure dips before switching to thermal.
switch_to_rgb_s_reason: Require sustained image recovery before switching back.
health_max_gap_s_reason: Reset hysteresis across missing frame stretches.
person_min_c_reason: Allow cooler exposed human skin or clothing.
person_max_c_reason: Reject fire and hot objects above human temperature.
person_min_area_m2_reason: Reject small warm objects and pixel noise.
person_max_area_m2_reason: Reject warm walls and large connected regions.
person_min_pixels_reason: Reject tiny components even if depth implies a large area.
blob_depth_jump_m_reason: Separate warm regions with incompatible depths.
candidate_window_s_reason: Require the repeated observations within one second.
person_confirm_max_range_m_reason: An agent may confirm a survivor only from an inspection within this range; farther, it must approach and look again. Re-measured after people became solid to the depth camera (22 Oct): over the 10 person verdicts on real people in one-door runs 923 to 925, ranges 2.6 to 5.0 m, the confirmed position would have been 0.13 to 0.50 m from the person, under half the 1.05 m scoring radius (n = 10, so a small sample). Before that fix a 6.55 m colour-only confirmation landed 1.55 m off; that case is still outside this range. The old 4.0 m limit refused 6 of 11 real person verdicts in 924 to 926, and the approaches that followed were lost to fire.
survivor_merge_m_reason: Report a person only once within the requested merge radius.
survivor_standoff_m_reason: A closer look stops this far from the warm shape. The thermal camera (sensors.json: 41 deg vertical view, pitched 10 deg down, 1.6 m up) sees the floor only from 1.6 / tan(30.5 deg) = 2.72 m ahead of the lens, 2.97 m from the robot centre (lens 0.25 m forward); nearer, a lying or slumped body is partly below its view, which left run 926's robot B 1.2 m from a person with no thermal view of her. 3.3 m keeps the whole body in thermal and colour view and inside the 5.0 m confirmation range.
survivor_stop_min_m_reason: A viewing stop closer than this does not count: the thermal camera's floor view starts 2.97 m from the robot centre (see survivor_standoff_m), so nearer stops cut off the lower body that the inspection needs.
survivor_stop_max_m_reason: A viewing stop farther than this does not count: inside search_max_range_m (4.0 m, where floor counts as searched) and 1.0 m inside person_confirm_max_range_m (5.0 m), for localisation and measurement error.
survivor_face_tolerance_deg_reason: Require the camera to face the person.
agent_arrival_hold_s_reason: After arriving where an agent asked (and facing the point it named), hold still this long for the agent's next order. The agent is asked at the arrival itself (RecordingSession.AgentDue) and the simulation pauses while it answers, so the hold covers only fresh camera frames (15 Hz) with margin. It was 5 s while arrivals waited out a 4 s gap between agent calls: on held-out seeds 915 to 917 that left robots standing 28 to 58 s per run after agent turns.
survivor_dwell_s_reason: Hold a stopped view for three seconds.
survivor_fresh_s_reason: Require recent thermal evidence throughout inspection.
survivor_lost_s_reason: Resume exploration if a candidate disappears.
retreat_reduced_clearance_reason: With no cool route at the full fire clearance, a retreat retries at emergency_fire_clearance_m and then last_resort_fire_clearance_m, never through a burning cell, and keeps that clearance while it follows the route. Held-out run 2 (seed 913), robot A: 'No safe cool route is known; hold position', then 70 s still in 381 C air with everything around it inside the 1.2 m fire margin (issue list 23 Oct, item 5). Test: fire lines 2.2 m apart, the robot between them retreats along the band; control holds.
agent_order_priority_reason: While an agent order other than exploring holds the robot (go_to, a turn to face, an arrival hold), the reflex leaves a fresh warm candidate to the agent for agent_candidate_grace_s, and leaves one the agent is walking to face for as long as that order lasts. Held-out runs 1 and 2: the reflex approach pre-empted 5 live agent orders (issue list 23 Oct, item 2). Explore orders do not hold it, and after the grace the reflex still walks up, since agent approaches were refused or dropped 15 times in those runs. Without an agent (headless, reflex-only runs) nothing changes; after 3 failed agent calls in a row the robot confirms people itself again.
agent_candidate_grace_s_reason: One or two agent steps: a model round is about 3 s (median 2.8 s, held-out runs 1 and 2) and a step about 13 s end to end, but the step that a candidate wakes starts at once and its first rounds decide whether to approach.
survivor_lost_in_view_reason: A collapsed person does not move: survivor_lost_s runs only while the candidate's spot is inside the camera's view (horizontal half-angle, past the blind floor for a body search_low_m high, within person_rgb_max_range_m, a known-free line on the robot's own map), and the approach is capped at 2 x person_rgb_max_range_m / near_speed_mps (40 s). Headless held-out houses 5005-5010 (23 Oct): 24 people seen, 13 confirmed; in house 5007 all five were seen and one confirmed, approaches ending as 'evidence was lost' while the spot was out of view behind furniture or a door frame. On since 23 Oct 17:25: tuning houses (exp8, selection) confirmed 4.5 to 4.8 of 5; held-out houses 5005-5010 (confirmation) 2.2 to 4.0, 0 false.
survivor_stop_speed_mps_reason: Use measured odometry to reject a moving inspection.
standoff_samples_reason: Search several approach directions around a survivor.
replan_s_reason: Refresh paths once per simulation second.
frontier_min_distance_m_reason: Avoid selecting a frontier under the current body.
frontier_gain_weight_reason: Nearest worthwhile frontier first, so an area is finished before moving on; the old 0.04 let a large unknown region 15 m away beat an unseen corner 2 m away.
frontier_information_radius_cells_reason: Count nearby unknown cells as information gain.
lookahead_m_reason: Follow the local path without cutting doorway corners.
goal_tolerance_m_reason: Allow grid quantization when reaching a waypoint.
escape_check_s_reason: How often a searching robot plans its route home to check that the way out is still open.
escape_fire_margin_m_reason: Fire this close to the route home means it is about to close: planned routes already keep fire_clearance_m (1.2 m) away, and the house fire spreads at about 1 m2 per second (agent run 11), so the robot returns while it still can.
heat_cool_after_s_reason: A cell this robot's own thermal camera sees cooler, with no hot reading for this long, takes the cooler value (fire put out or burnt out). Flames flicker within a fraction of a second and keep refreshing their hot reading, so a burning cell stays hot.
heat_emergency_fraction_reason: Below this heat budget, with no exit reachable at the normal fire clearance, the robot takes an emergency exit (2x2 building run: robot A sat beside its entry with the budget at 0).
emergency_fire_clearance_m_reason: Fire clearance for an emergency exit only: the body (0.25 m radius) passes a burning cell with about a quarter metre to spare, never through it.
last_resort_fire_clearance_m_reason: Fire clearance for an emergency exit when even emergency_fire_clearance_m shuts every way out: the body's own radius (0.25 m), so it passes beside burning cells, never through them. Held-out seed 914, robot B: with the route shut at 0.5 m it stood still in the foyer for 15 s while its air went from 26 to 52 C; a few seconds next to flames cost less than that.
escape_time_factor_reason: Leave when the fire, at the rate it is closing on the route home, would reach the route's planning clearance before the robot could walk out with this much spare: walking time is route length over open_speed_mps, and turns, doors and slowing near heat make the real walk up to about half as long again. Run 21: the fixed 2 m margin fired 2.4 s before robot B's hallway route closed; it was trapped for 137 s, 89 s above 60 C, 592 C peak.
escape_rate_window_s_reason: The closing rate needs the last three way-out checks spanning at least this long, and is the smaller of their two intervals' rates, so fire seen for the first time nearer the route (one jump) does not read as a fast front (run 22: robot A left at 10 s with fire 6 m from its route before this).
escape_recheck_s_reason: After the way out is lost, wait this long before checking it again, so a route that reopens next to the fire does not start a return that is cut again at once.
escape_ignore_m_reason: The first part of the route, within this distance of the robot, is left to the avoid margins; only fire further along the way out ends the search.
return_arrive_m_reason: A returning robot is back once within this distance of its start. The start is usually an entry doorway, narrower than the planning clearance, so the return path ends up to about half a metre short of it.
open_speed_mps_reason: Use the requested exploration speed in open space.
near_speed_mps_reason: Slow down in doorways and near occupied cells.
near_obstacle_m_reason: Use the slow speed before a narrow passage.
near_cone_deg_reason: Check side clearance as well as the forward ray.
goal_slow_distance_m_reason: Reduce speed before stopping at a goal.
thermal_speed_mps_reason: Limit travel speed while colour is unreliable.
turn_in_place_deg_reason: Above this heading error, straight pursuit needs either a checked body arc or a stationary turn. In tight or unobserved space, brake before rotating and retain the capsule swing check.
arc_max_heading_deg_reason: Permit checked arcs only while the goal remains in the forward half plane, including a quarter turn; a goal behind the body still needs a pivot. At open walking speed 0.6 m/s and the 60 deg/s yaw limit, the centre turns at radius 0.573 m. With body_half_length_m 0.375 and body_radius_m 0.18, the outer capsule reaches about sqrt(0.573^2+0.195^2)+0.18=0.785 m from the turn centre. ArcSafe checks that moving capsule in known free cells, with the actual speed ramp, heat margins and a straight braking corridor at every sample. An indoor robot under stay_inside also needs proven indoor floor along the arc and its braking corridor. Sampling moves the furthest body point at most a quarter cell and adds half that spacing plus each cell's half diagonal as a clearance bound. Zero restores stop-and-turn above turn_in_place_deg for comparison. OFF (0) as shipped, 22 Oct 20:05: with arcs on, two EditMode tests regressed (wall-following outside made 1.7 m of the 7 m it should, and a carried person was set down 1.56 m instead of at least 1.6 m from the way out); keep turning in place until those are fixed.
heading_gain_reason: Close heading errors without requesting excessive yaw.
collision_stop_m_reason: Radius of the near-obstacle slow zone check; emergency limits use the swept body circle (collision_margin_m).
collision_cone_deg_reason: Legacy cone, used only to bound near_cone_deg.
scan_yaw_dps_reason: Inspect unseen directions at a bounded turn rate.
no_frontier_scan_s_reason: Allow a full look around before declaring exploration exhausted.
heat_drain_start_c_reason: Start spending the heat budget above fifty degrees.
heat_drain_per_degree_s_reason: Spend four percent per second at seventy degrees.
heat_recover_per_s_reason: Recover a depleted budget over tens of cool seconds.
heat_retreat_fraction_reason: Retreat before the budget is exhausted.
heat_resume_fraction_reason: Require substantial recovery before exploring again.
retreat_min_distance_m_reason: Choose a cooler location away from the current exposure.
mission_time_limit_s_reason: Bound exploration to the C14 four minute target before returning.
survivor_stop_yaw_dps_reason: Require low measured yaw rate before counting a stationary inspection.
retreat_start_weight_reason: Prefer an equally cool cell nearer the estimated start.
retreat_path_weight_reason: Break cool-target ties with a shorter reachable path.
retreat_air_weight_reason: Staying inside, retreat floor is scored by the air this robot measured near it (degrees above ambient, same units as the surface heat term), from its own track. A hot gas layer heats the air long before the floor shows on the thermal map: seed 929, robot B stood still at its 'coolest floor' by surface heat while its air rose to 47 C, having measured 20 C in the foyer 40 s earlier. Floor with no sample near it counts as hot as the air where the robot stands, so the robot does not gamble on floor it has never measured.
air_sample_radius_m_reason: An air reading stands for floor within 1 m of where it was taken: about the body length, and air in a room mixes over metres, not centimetres.
fire_near_m_reason: The nozzle's throw (actuators.json nozzle.range_m, 5.0 m). With the robot's own air at or above air_warm_c, the nearest floor it measured burning within this distance is offered to the agent as a spray option, whether or not that fire blocks a route: seed 929 robot B's air rose from 30 to 211 C beside a fire in its own room and it was never offered its 12 L of water.
air_sample_spacing_m_reason: Keep one air sample per half metre walked (the newest replaces the last one within that distance), so a robot standing still does not fill its track with one spot.
fixed_grid_origin_reason: Each robot's grid is centred on where it entered; it has no building coordinates.
frontier_gain_cap_cells_reason: Cap the size bonus at 1.5 m^2 of unknown floor so distance decides between worthwhile frontiers.
frontier_min_information_cells_reason: Ignore unknown slivers under 0.1 m^2 (under furniture, wall seams) that cameras cannot resolve and that held robots in place.
visited_radius_m_reason: A reached frontier spot is not chosen again within this radius.
visited_hold_s_reason: How long a reached spot stays set aside; after that the robot may return if unknown floor is still there.
sweep_spacing_m_reason: Sweep once per new area: no second sweep within 3 m.
sweep_repeat_s_reason: A sweep older than this no longer counts for the spacing rule.
sweep_hold_s_reason: Minimum hold of each look, long enough for several thermal and depth frames (15 Hz). The brain holds longer when the colour detector needs it: person_rgb_sightings x person_rgb_scan_period_s (2 s), so two colour scans fall inside one look whatever their phase.
sweep_yaw_dps_reason: Turn fast enough to keep sweeps short, under the 60 deg/s body limit.
sweep_tolerance_deg_reason: Heading accuracy for each look of the sweep.
area_report_radius_m_reason: Radius for the coverage figure reported after each sweep.
progress_min_cells_reason: 0.4 m^2 of newly mapped floor per window counts as progress.
progress_window_s_reason: Exploring this long without progress means the robot is circling.
progress_min_travel_m_reason: The progress watchdog counts the robot as circling only if it travelled at least this far in the window. Over 15 s a robot circling at the 0.3 m/s doorway speed covers 4.5 m; one turning in place or held between agent orders covers under 0.2 m of odometry drift. Held-out seed 914 run 4: robot A, turning in place to face warm shapes, had a 2.5 m circle set aside around its doorway, which held the open door of an unsearched bedroom 2.3 m away.
exit_open_share_reason: A cell is open beyond when at least this share of the sweeps whose beams crossed it came back with nothing within the LiDAR's 12 m. Smoke drops each pulse on its own, at most half of them (sensors.json smoke_dropout.max), so a cell whose beams return off a wall reads open about half the time at worst: 27 or more open sweeps of 30 then has probability 3e-6. Measured (held-out seed 914 run 5, robot A in the foyer, 450 sweeps): 77.7 % of beams through the front door returned nothing, against 4.2 % at the wall beside it; past the doorway, where blocked beams no longer count, the share is near 100 %.
exit_min_scans_reason: Sweeps (3 s at 10 Hz) that must have crossed a cell before its open share counts; with exit_open_share it bounds a false exit from smoke at 3e-6 per cell.
exit_max_count_reason: Sensed ways out kept per robot; 0 switches the LiDAR exit detector off. Switched off 22 Oct 10:15 after its first live run (held-out seed 918): within 30 s it registered ways out inside the house, on hallway floor for robot A and in the study for robot B, because the LiDAR's 12 m range also reads nothing along a 20 m hallway or into a room whose far wall is 12.5 m away, the same as through an exterior door. The synthetic test room (6 m) could not show that. It needs a second cue, the camera seeing sky rather than ceiling, before it can certify a way out.
burning_radius_m_reason: Burning floor counted around the point where fire blocks the way (fire_blocks_exit / fire_blocks_frontier burning_m2): within the nozzle's narrow-fog footprint at its 5 m throw (12 deg half-angle covers about 2 m), so the area is what one aimed stream would have to knock down.
threshold_exit_clear_m_reason: A doorway look (RobotBrain.ThresholdLook) is never taken from within this distance of a known way out: there the unproven floor beyond is the yard the robot walked in from. 1.5 m is a door width plus the 0.375 m half body length either side, so the front-door threshold is skipped and an interior doorway one room in is not.
teammate_predict_max_s_reason: A partner's body is predicted from its last radioed pose for at most this long (OnTeammate): two 2 s message intervals, so one lost message still leaves it masked. Heard from longer ago it may be anywhere, and its returns are mapped as usual.
teammate_mask_margin_m_reason: Beyond the body's 0.375 m half length, LiDAR and depth returns this close to the partner's predicted stretch are its body: B's placement error at the pad is sigma 5 cm and 2 deg (3 sigma 0.15 m plus 0.1 m of heading at 3 m), and odometry adds a few cm. Masking only skips returns; it erases nothing already mapped.
survivor_view_clear_m_reason: A viewing standpoint needs no mapped wall on its line to the person, except within this distance of the person: a body slumped against a wall or lying by furniture is itself in the map, or touches wall cells, there. Half a metre is a seated person's depth from the wall to the front of the knees.
wait_behind_partner_s_reason: Longest a robot waits behind a partner standing just ahead on the way in (WaitBehindPartner) before its no-frontier scan may end the search: two agent steps (up to about 13 s each in run 924), so a partner stopped to inspect or confirm someone has moved on. Seed 925: A stood 6 s confirming a person in the doorway and B, with nothing else reachable, ended its mission at 18 s.
threshold_look_options_reason: Unproven frontiers checked per decision for a doorway to look through, best score first. Each tried frontier is remembered, so later decisions reach the rest; eight bounds the planning work of one tick (each is already planned by the frontier search).
follow_partner_standoff_m_reason: Following a partner in through the one door, stop this far short of where it was last heard: two body lengths, so the two do not crowd a doorway, and the follower's camera (which sees the floor from 2.16 m) looks past the partner onto new floor.
rendezvous_after_s_reason: Out of radio contact this long before walking back to where the partner was last heard (RobotBrain.RendezvousStep). Held-out seeds 919 and 920: out of contact 168 to 184 s of 200, each robot searching blind to the other's map. 45 s is about a quarter of the mission: long enough to search a room or two between meetings, short enough for two meetings.
rendezvous_min_unshared_cells_reason: Only walk back with at least this much own map (0.1 m cells, so 15 square metres, about a room) the partner has not acknowledged: a meeting for a few cells costs more search time than it returns.
rendezvous_hold_s_reason: Wait this long where the partner was last heard before searching on: five 2 s radio broadcasts, so a partner walking back over the same interval is heard if it is coming.
exterior_dwell_s_reason: A robot that left for safety and is allowed back in waits outside this long, while the re-entry check runs every escape_check_s (seven checks), before it follows the building's wall to look for another way in; 0 switches that off. DARPA SubT: CERBERUS backtracks after a set time without motion and GBPlanner2 keeps exploring when home is unreachable. Held-out seeds 916 and 917: robots stood at their own blocked door for 106 to 124 s.
facade_band_m_reason: Outside, the robot moves only to floor within this distance of a wall it has mapped: along the building, never into open yard, so the wall stays in its LiDAR's view for localisation (held-out run 2: robot B lost its position searching an open yard). Robot radius 0.25 m plus a 1.2 m fire clearance leaves room to pass a burning doorway at about this distance.
progress_skip_radius_m_reason: Frontiers this close to a no-progress spot are set aside.
sweep_max_s_reason: A sweep that has not finished in 16 s ends, so no wall or turn conflict can hold the robot. A full sweep turns 240 degrees at sweep_yaw_dps 45 (5.3 s) and holds three looks of 2 s (6 s), 11.3 s; 16 s leaves time for settling within sweep_tolerance_deg.
collision_escape_s_reason: A collision stop that lasts 3 s without the path clearing becomes a stall: back up, turn, and set the goal aside after repeats.
collision_margin_m_reason: Forward speed is capped so the body can brake to a stop this far short of the first occupied cell its circle would sweep into.
lead_max_m_reason: A robot standing closer to something than the planning clearance steps out through cells the body fits in, up to this far, then plans from the first walkable cell.
agent_avoid_min_radius_m_reason: Smallest keep-out circle an agent's avoid_area may draw: three cells, so it shows on the map. An area that would have to shrink below this to leave the robot outside is refused.
agent_avoid_max_radius_m_reason: Largest keep-out circle: about one room, so one model call cannot close off the house.
scan_yaw_gain_reason: Apply 5 percent of each own-map scan heading correction. M1 fixed-motion replay with the interval fix found gain 1 improved robot B in seed 934, but worsened run 13 robot A yaw maximum from 0.793 to 2.314 degrees and position maximum from 0.223 to 0.573 m. Keep 0.05 because gain 1 regresses run 13. See M1_REPORT.txt.
scan_beam_stride_reason: Use every third LiDAR beam for matching (240 of 720).
scan_min_beams_reason: Fewer valid returns than this and the sweep is not matched.
scan_match_range_m_reason: Returns beyond this range are not matched; far returns amplify small angle errors.
scan_sigma_m_reason: Width of the Gaussian that scores how close a beam endpoint lands to a mapped wall.
scan_window_m_reason: Search the corrected position within this many metres of the odometry prediction, per sweep (10 Hz).
scan_step_m_reason: Position step of the correlative search.
scan_window_deg_reason: Search heading within this many degrees of the prediction.
scan_step_deg_reason: Heading step of the correlative search.
scan_min_fit_reason: Mean endpoint score needed before a correction is trusted (0 to 1).
scan_softness_reason: Candidates within a few of these of the best score are averaged, so a featureless corridor keeps the prediction along its axis.
localization_report_s_reason: Log a localization summary (matched sweeps, mean fit, summed correction) this often.
frontier_cluster_max_m_reason: A frontier cluster grows at most this far from its first cell, so a long edge of unsearched floor (common once the LiDAR maps whole rooms) becomes several targets the agent can choose between.
search_requires_ceiling_reason: Robots get no building outline or map. They search only floor where their own camera has seen a ceiling overhead, which keeps them out of the yard and rejects warm shapes seen through windows (Tashon, 2026-10-20: no prior layout knowledge).
ceiling_min_height_m_reason: Depth points this high and up count as ceiling: above door lintels (about 2.1 m) and every obstacle the brain maps (up to 1.9 m).
ceiling_sight_lines_reason: Floor on a known-free straight line from an indoor camera to ceiling it saw is under that ceiling, so it is indoors. The camera sees ceiling only about 4.7 m away, and the 0.6 m ceiling radius alone hid most of small rooms (agent run 14: 454 study cells, where a person lay). A camera in the yard marks nothing, and lines stop at walls and unmapped floor.
ceiling_radius_m_reason: Floor within 0.6 m (walked across free floor) of ceiling evidence is indoors. Evidence sits at least ceiling_wall_margin_m inside the walls, so 0.6 m reaches the floor along inner walls but not yard floor beyond a doorway (run 8: robot B targeted 0.65 m outside its door with 1.5 m).
ceiling_min_hits_reason: A cell needs this many ceiling returns, so one noisy depth pixel does not make the yard indoors.
enclosure_rays_reason: Rays cast from a cell through the robot's own map to test whether it is walled in (every 10 degrees).
enclosure_range_m_reason: A ray that reaches a wall within this distance counts as closed; one that runs this far over floor mapped free counts as open. Longer than the house's rooms and corridors, shorter than the 12 m LiDAR range.
enclosure_min_closed_share_reason: A cell is walled in when at least this share of rays reach a wall. Rays into unmapped space count as neither, so a room partly hidden behind door jambs still qualifies.
frontier_peek_m_reason: Unsearched floor this far past a standable cell, reached only through cells too tight for the body (a gap beside furniture, a strip along a wall), still makes that standable cell a frontier, so the robot goes there and looks in. The strip next to any obstacle is robot_radius_m plus half a cell diagonal (0.32 m) wide, and furniture a person can hide behind is about 0.6 to 0.9 m deep; 1.2 m covers both. Hidden-corner run: a woman behind a desk across a kitchen corner had no standable cell next to her floor, so no frontier was ever offered. The same local reach bounds a doorway evidence move, each search for a mapped wall jamb, and the clear line back to prior indoor evidence. The body stops its calibrated camera offset inside the wall line. The synthetic 1.2 m opening fixture measures travel under this 1.2 m bound; openings whose jambs lie beyond that reach remain ordinary agent options. Evidence looks use the existing sweep_max_s and sweep_hold_s limits.
enclosure_max_open_share_reason: And at most this share run out over open mapped ground. Open ground has most of its rays open (or ending in unmapped space, which counts as neither). Through a 1 m open outside door, a room cell 2 m inside sees open ground in about 8 percent of directions and is walled in; cells within about 1.5 m of such a door are not (14 percent at 1 m) and need the ceiling rule.
lidar_open_span_deg_reason: A span of at least this many degrees of neighbouring LiDAR beams with no return is open ground: nothing within the LiDAR's 12 m that way. Smoke loses each pulse on its own, at most half of them (sensors.json smoke_dropout.max), so 60 empty beams in a row by chance has odds under 1e-18. Inside the house the widest empty span is a doorway seen from close up or the far end of the 20 m hallway (about 10 degrees from 2 m inside one end); in the yard it is about 140 degrees. Rays of the enclosure test run on across open ground instead of stopping as unknown (held-out run 2: one long facade plus the person robot B had carried out made the yard walled in).
air_warm_c_reason: Air at the mast this warm means the hot gas layer has reached the robot (ambient 20 C plus 10). In all 15 recorded robot runs where the air later passed 60 C it first read 30 C 10 to 94 s before (air_rise check, 2026-10-21). Used only when the robot is already in trouble (no reachable frontier left, or cut off from its way out): as a leave trigger on its own it fired in 15 of 33 runs that stayed safe, because robots walk from the yard into halls already at 25 to 45 C.
air_rise_c_per_min_reason: Rate-of-rise heat detectors (UL 521, NFPA 72) alarm at 15 F (8.3 C) per minute, the rise of a growing compartment fire. Same scope as air_warm_c. Held-out run 2: robot A's air rose about 45 C/min from 95 s while its agent kept it beside the fire; its way out closed at 114 s.
air_rise_window_s_reason: The rise is the least-squares slope over this window of the robot's own thermocouple (10 Hz, 0.3 C noise): about 0.6 C/min of slope error, 7 percent of air_rise_c_per_min. The window must be at least 80 percent covered.
air_rise_min_delta_c_reason: And the air must be at least this far above the robot's lowest reading of the last air_rise_baseline_s, so a short wiggle in steady cool air is not a rise.
air_rise_baseline_s_reason: The baseline for air_rise_min_delta_c: the robot's lowest air reading over the last minute.
fire_cut_blacklist_s_reason: A frontier whose planned path the fire margin cut is not chosen again for this long. Flames flicker: a cell seen cooler for heat_cool_after_s (2 s) drops out of the margin, so the same frontier kept returning (held-out seed 914, robot A: chosen and cut three times in 4 s beside a burning doorway, no_frontier restarted each time and the scan never ended). 20 s is long against the flicker and short against the run, so a fire that is out can be searched past later.
reenter_after_heat_s_reason: After leaving because heat was building (a heat return or an emergency exit), wait this long outside, in cool and steady air, before going back in; once back in, heat building makes it leave at once. From outside the robot cannot see whether the hot layer has cleared, and a compartment's hot layer persists while the fire burns (held-out seed 914 run 1: robot A re-entered 0.1 s after its emergency exit, into the hallway it had just left with its air at 34 C and rising). 30 s is a few escape checks and short against a 200 s search.
candidate_wall_extent_m_reason: A thermal-only candidate whose spot touches an occupied structure at least this long on the robot's own map is flagged on_wall: the robot does not approach it on its own and the agent is told. Measured over 15 recorded runs (tools/candidate_wall_eval.py): 2 of 203 thermal candidates were people (colour candidates: 13 of 16); 150 of the 201 others lay on a structure of 2 m or more (walls heated by the fire), and so did 1 of the 2 people (a person lying against a wall, slow-fire run). Not dropped, because of that person: the agent can still inspect it from where the robot stands.
candidate_wall_disc_m_reason: Occupied cells this close to the candidate's position count as the structure it lies on (about a body half-width).
candidate_wall_window_m_reason: The structure is followed at most this far from the candidate in x and y, enough to see a wall run past 2 m.
survivor_keepout_m_reason: Around each person this robot has confirmed (its own estimate), the planner treats a disc of this radius as an obstacle: half a 1.7 m adult body lying in any direction (0.85 m) plus the 0.2 m the body's nose reaches beyond its 0.18 m radius. The walking clearance (robot_radius_m) is added by the planner on top. Seed 927: robot A routed past the person it had just confirmed, pressed into her, and was pinned from 46 s.
survivor_keepout_core_m_reason: The hard part of the keep-out around a confirmed person: half an adult's shoulder width (0.23 m) plus the measured confirmation position error (0.13 to 0.50 m over 10 real person verdicts; about 0.2 m typical). The body surely lies within it whichever way it lies. Beyond it, out to survivor_keepout_m, the floor costs extra instead of being forbidden: seed 931 confirmed a person 2.4 m inside the one door, and the whole 1.05 m disc as an obstacle closed the entrance to both robots.
keepout_cost_weight_reason: Path cost per cell at the edge of the keep-out core, falling quadratically to 0 at survivor_keepout_m. Crossing the ring costs more than walking about 4 m around it, so through open floor routes still keep the full disc clear (seed 927 pinning); a robot passes close only where the ring is the only way.
entrance_lock_m_reason: Owner's rule (23 Oct): once inside, a robot never goes back to, or near, the way it came in. The way in is the first point where the robot's own track stood on floor it had proven indoors; once the robot is this far beyond it, floor within this distance of it is an obstacle for every route and goal. 2.5 m (owner's choice) keeps the 1.6 m camera out of the doorway, so it never stands looking out at the yard (seed 932: robot B's retreat ended 1 m inside the front door), while the rest of the first room stays searchable.
heat_steer_radius_m_reason: Staying inside, a fast rise in the robot's own air sets aside floor within this distance of where it stands, so the search goes on elsewhere: about half a room, the area whose air the robot just measured warming. It replaces the old rule that held the robot still: in seed 932 that rule fired at about 24 C and the robots spent 62 s and 66 s retreating in air below 50 C.
heat_steer_s_reason: How long that floor stays set aside: three air_rise_window_s periods, long enough to search a room elsewhere before checking the warming area again with fresh air readings.
entrance_lock_passage_reason: The entrance lock stays an obstacle only on floor not proven indoors, so no route leaves by the way in; the indoor part of the disc becomes a passage that costs entrance_lock_cost_weight per cell and is never a goal (no frontier, standoff, retreat or threshold look stops there). Headless house 5015 (23 Oct): the way in opened onto the hallway 1.2 m from the living room door; the whole-disc lock walled both robots into the living room, both stood still 318 s, 8 of 9 rooms went unsearched. The same seal held one robot in its first side room for the whole run in houses 5013, 5014 and 5016. Headless exp10 (240 s, off vs on): 5015 coverage 15 to 85 %, confirmed 1 to 5 of 5, standing 318 to 40 s; tuning 5001-5004 mean coverage 77 to 80.5 %, standing 82 to 47 s, confirmed 19 to 18 of 20 (5003: second person in the study seen at 197 s, its approach cut by the 240 s clock), 0 false either way.
entrance_lock_cost_weight_reason: Added per cell crossed on the entrance passage, on top of the travel cost of 1: crossing 3 m of passage weighs like a 60 m detour, so routes cross it only when no other way leads on. Same scale as keepout_cost_weight at a person's core edge.
stay_inside_reason: Owner's decision (22 Oct 2026): a robot that has gone in never leaves by the entrance. At the mission deadline it stops where it stands; heat, a closing way out or nothing left to search make it retreat to the coolest floor proven indoors (no pull to the start, which is outside), where it can spray its finite water and wait for the air to cool. No way-out watch and no emergency exit run.
frames_shared_at_start_reason: Each robot starts in its own frame without an operator pose. LiDAR and camera candidates must pass own LiDAR map fit, uniqueness, and two separated agreeing matches before partner content applies (Tashon, 2026-10-20; data/evidence/place_recognition_eval.json).
keyframe_spacing_m_reason: Keep a LiDAR keyframe every metre walked.
keyframe_beams_reason: Keyframes keep every other beam (360), 720 bytes on the radio.
keyframe_max_reason: Keyframes kept per robot and per partner.
keyframes_per_message_reason: Each map packet carries the newest unsent keyframe and one older one in turn, so lost ones are resent.
link_shortlist_reason: Own keyframes with the closest ring keys get the full fingerprint comparison.
link_max_candidates_reason: Unconfirmed link candidates kept per partner.
link_max_descriptor_distance_reason: Mean relative range difference (0 to 1) between two keyframes' range profiles below which they may be the same place; the map check then decides.
link_window_m_reason: A candidate is verified by placing the partner's sweep in this map within this distance of the matched keyframe.
link_step_m_reason: Coarse position step of the wide verification search; the per-sweep matcher then refines at 2.5 cm.
link_window_deg_reason: Heading window around each fingerprint turn: two 6 degree sectors either side, so the true turn is inside even when the best shifts straddle it (test: shifts 28 and 32 around a true 30).
link_step_deg_reason: Coarse heading step of the wide search; refined by the per-sweep matcher.
link_min_fit_reason: Mean beam score needed for a verified place match.
link_agree_m_reason: Two matches must give transforms this close in position...
link_agree_deg_reason: ...and in heading before the frames are linked.
link_min_separation_m_reason: The two agreeing matches must come from partner keyframes at least this far apart, so one ambiguous spot cannot link the maps alone.
link_turn_candidates_reason: Verify the three best fingerprint turns in the map, not only the best: rectangular rooms look alike turned 180 degrees.
keyframe_min_return_share_reason: Only keyframes with returns in at least 60 % of directions link maps: out in the yard most beams hit nothing and two empty sweeps look alike (check run 3: a false yard match at fingerprint distance 0.08).
link_unique_shift_m_reason: A verified placement is tested again shifted this far in four directions...
link_unique_ratio_reason: ...and rejected if any shift scores above 85 % of the placement's fit: one straight wall fits anywhere along it.
link_verifications_per_step_reason: At most this many map verifications per brain step, so fingerprint linking cannot stall the 60 Hz loop (check run 3 slowed to 3.6 sim s per minute).
link_coarse_min_fit_reason: The coarse 10 cm / 2 degree search only has to find the neighbourhood; a candidate needs this fit there, then link_min_fit after fine refinement.
link_diagnostics_reason: Log every rejected fingerprint comparison (place_rejected) during the overnight verification runs; turn off for the final demo runs.
ceiling_wall_margin_m_reason: Ceiling evidence counts only on cells at least this far from a mapped wall: wall faces reach the ceiling height band, and their noisy points outside an exterior wall made the yard look roofed (run 6). 0.4 m is under half the narrowest hallway.
person_rgb_min_confidence_reason: YOLO11m (OpenCV 5 dnn) confidence needed for a colour person sighting; the agent's inspect_candidate uses the same 0.5. Measured by rgb_people_eval on 17,816 frames of 9 recordings (4 distinct visible survivor positions, 24 visible episodes): with 2 sightings in 3 s, candidates are 182 true, 1 false over 15 sampling phases (precision 0.995, worst recording 0.980), episode recall 0.48. At 0.6: 171 true, 0 false, recall 0.44. 0.5 kept because the agent inspects every candidate before confirming.
person_rgb_max_range_m_reason: Sightings farther than this are ignored: the box depth gets unreliable and the person is too small to confirm. Measured: per-frame precision at confidence 0.5 is 0.91 at 4 to 6 m and 0.44 beyond 6 m.
person_rgb_sightings_reason: Two colour sightings of one place within person_rgb_window_s make a survivor candidate.
person_rgb_window_s_reason: Window for repeated colour sightings (scans run once per second).
person_rgb_fresh_s_reason: A colour track counts as currently seen for this long after a sighting (thermal tracks use survivor_fresh_s at 15 Hz).
person_rgb_scan_period_s_reason: The recorder runs the colour person detector on each robot's latest frame this often (661 ms per frame on the M5 CPU).
person_floor_clearance_m_reason: A thermal blob's median height must be at least this far above the floor: heated floor near a fire was a main source of false warm shapes (warm_eval).
person_top_max_m_reason: A thermal blob's 95th-percentile height must be under a standing adult's height plus margin; taller warm patches are walls. Not tuned to this scenario's poses (lying, slumped), so a standing person still passes.
see_over_clearance_m_reason: An obstacle whose top (from the live 3D map) is at least this far below the camera can be looked over when choosing where to look from. From a camera at height h the floor behind an object of height o, seen from d metres, is hidden for d*o/(h-o): at h 1.6 m and o up to 1.1 m that is at most 2.2 d, so a person sitting or lying behind a desk (0.75 m) or bed is partly in view over it, while a wardrobe, fridge or wall (1.8 m and up) is not. Hidden-corner run: the desk across the corner counted as a wall.
thermal_lidar_range_fallback_reason: When smoke removes the depth camera's return under a warm thermal pixel, take its range from the LiDAR beam at the same bearing, so thermal can still size a warm blob. Hidden-corner run 2: fluid smoke left 1 % valid depth at times and thermal confirmed nobody while the colour camera was blind too. Limit: the LiDAR plane is 0.45 m up, so it ranges sitting or slumped people but passes over someone lying flat (that blob then sizes too large and is rejected).
carried_person_radius_m_reason: Half the length of an adult lying down (about 1.7 m). A person carried out is set down this far plus a robot's width (2 x robot_radius_m) past the way out, so a robot can pass between the body and the door, and the robot marks a circle of this radius where it set them down as an obstacle in its own map. Hidden-corner run 1: s1 left 5 cm inside the front doorway trapped robot A outside for 156 of 200 s.
search_max_range_m_reason: Floor counts as searched only when the robot's camera saw it from within this distance; farther floor is mapped but stays a search target. It equals person_confirm_max_range_m: a person is confirmed only from an inspection within 4 m (rgb_people_eval: per-frame precision 0.93 up to 4 m, worse beyond), so floor seen from farther has not really been searched. Hidden-corner runs: the depth camera marked floor searched out to its 8 m range, a glance through a doorway counted a room as done, and the robot never went in. Sweep eligibility uses this same range and the camera calibration's horizontal field of view. A view of searched floor and opaque mapped obstacles adds no searched floor; unknown floor still keeps the look.
search_low_m_reason: Floor counts as searched only where a depth ray passes within this height of it, the height of an adult lying on the floor (about 0.25 to 0.4 m): a person lying there would have blocked the ray. A ray that passes higher, over a table or counter to the wall behind, still maps the floor free for driving but does not count it searched (held-out seed 914 run 1: 24.9 m2 was marked searched that no depth image ever showed, measured with tools/floor_seen.py, including the floor where a person lay slumped by the kitchen island). 0 restores the old rule.
frontier_beyond_m_reason: How far mapped_unsearched_m2 looks past a frontier: the LiDAR's maximum range (sensors.json lidar max_m), the farthest the robot's own map can reach from where it stood.
reject_new_view_deg_reason: A warm shape the agent rejected is raised again only once the robot sees it from this many degrees round from where it stood when rejecting it, or from half the distance; a colour person sighting lifts the rejection at once. From the same viewpoint a second look adds nothing (held-out seed 914 run 2: the rejected 38 C fridge was raised again in the same second, three times), while a new side can show a person the first view hid. 45 deg is a clearly different side of an object a metre or two across.
reject_share_s_reason: A warm spot one robot's agent inspected and rejected travels to the partner by radio. The partner treats it as rejected from where the first robot stood (same reject_new_view_deg rule) for this long. Seed 928: robots A and B inspected and rejected the same spot near (9.0, 6.4) four times between 43 and 74 s, because each rejection stayed on the robot that made it. 60 s covers that 31 s span with margin, and is short enough that a spot rejected before a fire changed the room gets a fresh look from the partner's own sensors.
frontier_wide_options_reason: Of the frontier options offered to the agent, up to this many go to the frontiers opening onto the largest distinct regions of mapped but unsearched floor (one per region); the rest stay nearest first. Nearest first alone filled the list with corners of the current room once floor behind furniture counted as unsearched (held-out seed 914 runs 3 and 4: 102 of 162 options in the robot's current room; in the foyer all six were corners while the doors to three unsearched rooms were not offered). 3 of 8 keeps most options local.
frontier_wide_min_m2_reason: A region needs this much mapped floor beyond its frontier to take a wide slot, including floor whose indoor status still needs the agent's OpenCV check. The minimum is about the floor an adult lying down covers (0.5 x 1.8 m), so a pocket too small to hide a person does not displace a nearby option.
route_watch_reason: Keep the existing search behaviour unless enabled for comparison. Held-out run 1 saw no fire cells from 96 to 116 s while the route home burned; the robot turned at 120 s and the way out closed 0.2 s later. Enabled from 22 Oct 01:55 to be measured in an integration run: offline it caught a 0.3 to 0.5 m/s hallway fire front in time 4 to 13 % of the time, so it is a second layer behind the heat rules.
route_watch_stale_s_reason: Held-out run 1 missed route fire for at least 20 s from 96 to 116 s. A 15 s stale look threshold checks before that measured blind interval.
route_watch_max_stale_share_reason: Require a majority of the route beyond escape_ignore_m to be unseen for 15 s. Held-out run 1 missed the fire along that route for 20 s; one unobserved cell should not turn the robot.
route_watch_min_interval_s_reason: Bound routine interruptions to one per 90 s. Held-out run 1 first needed the look during the 96 to 116 s blind interval; the 12 s cap then costs at most 12/90 of search time.
route_watch_dwell_s_reason: The closing-rate rule needs two intervals of escape_check_s=2 s after seeing fire. A 4.5 s dwell provides both plus 0.5 s for image delivery.
route_watch_max_s_reason: At sweep_yaw_dps=45 a half turn needs 4 s, plus the 4.5 s dwell. A 12 s cap leaves 3.5 s for heading convergence and delayed images without an unbounded stop.
visual_keyframe_period_s_reason: How often a robot asks its own OpenCV 5 place service for a camera keyframe (ORB features with positions). One per radio broadcast (2 s): at 0.3 to 0.5 m/s that is a keyframe every 0.6 to 1 m, closer than the 1.5 m within which two cameras still share most of a view.
visual_keyframe_max_reason: Own camera keyframes kept for sending (400 s of keyframes at one per 2 s, longer than a run).
visual_keyframes_per_message_reason: Send at most one 96-feature visual keyframe per broadcast, newest first and older views in turn. Its payload is 3653 bytes; with one LiDAR sweep MessageByteLimitsUseActualBinaryRoundTripsAtHouseScale measured full 7975 bytes and delta 7407 bytes.
visual_link_min_inliers_reason: Match the service floor in config/perception.json. place_eval database mode rejected the worst wrong checkerboard/tile match with 15 inliers by requiring 16. The measured evaluation had 0 false accepts in about 58000 negatives. Map verification and two separated candidates still apply.
visual_place_linking_reason: Enable camera proposals from the measured ORB service. tools/place_eval.py recorded 0 false accepts in about 58000 negative pairs, 4.6 percent cross-robot recall, and 2.4 cm median pose error. LiDAR map fit, uniqueness, and two separated agreeing candidates still gate every link.
visual_lidar_keyframes_per_message_reaso: MessageByteLimitsUseActualBinaryRoundTripsAtHouseScale measured an 8165-byte delta with two 360-beam LiDAR sweeps and one 96-feature visual payload, above 8000 bytes. One sweep near the visual capture pose supports map verification even after a delayed service reply. The test measured 7407-byte deltas and 7975-byte full snapshots; LiDAR-only messages still carry two.
visual_keyframe_max_payload_bytes_reason: The measured service uses 96 ORB features at 38 bytes each plus a 5-byte header, exactly 3653 bytes. Reject larger service payloads until the radio budget is measured again; the one-sweep house delta measured 7407 bytes.
reentry_requires_interior_link_reason: After walking outside, re-enter only ceiling-backed free floor connected indoors to floor this robot searched before leaving. A free yard path and a neighbouring ceiling do not establish the same structure. Uses body clearance and four-neighbour map connectivity, without a gate-distance cutoff, outline or house identity. Missing roof coverage can conservatively leave a real alternative entrance unverified.
frontier_local_evidence_reason: Before leaving the camera's search_max_range_m horizon, take a bounded look from proven own floor at nearby mapped unsearched floor whose indoor status is unknown. Run 926 A at 75 s had 5.35 m2 of mapped unsearched bedroom floor but only 0.30 m2 proven indoors; waiting until no proven frontier remained postponed the evidence needed to enter. The target comes from connected unsearched cells in the robot's map, at least frontier_wide_min_m2 in area so a wall sliver does not interrupt a search. It uses no room labels or complete jambs. Travel cost and the sight line each stay within search_max_range_m, the camera search distance. Unknown cells block body travel but do not block a camera look; mapped walls block both. After one attempt, resume the interrupted frontier until the robot moves visited_radius_m to a new standpoint. The calibrated camera field of view and sweep_repeat_s also suppress repeated views; sweep_hold_s and sweep_max_s bound dwell. Known exits, claims, exclusions, heat and explicit agent approaches still win. A look never marks indoor or searched floor. Off since 23 Oct 17:25: with room_indoor_promotion the robot's own enclosed rooms are proven without the look; headless tuning houses 5001-5004 (exp7, selection) mean room searched 67.5 to 78.8 %, turning 103 to 89 s, stuck events 19 to 2.8 with this off and sweep_once_per_room on.
frontier_doorway_looks_reason: An explore_frontier order chooses search floor, so the same bounded doorway camera look available during reflex exploration remains available en route. Explicit go_to/person approaches and holds still take precedence. Uses the existing body/camera geometry, frontier_peek_m, sweep_hold_s and sweep_max_s; no house-specific timing or direction is added.
room_ledger_reason: Opt-in room priority from sensed free floor only. On since 23 Oct 16:50: headless simulator, 10 random houses at 240 s (6 held out, never tuned on), together with the five switches below: mean room searched 56 to 70 % on the held-out houses, rooms under half searched 3.8 to 2.0 per house, standing halved, 0 false confirmations (data/runs/headless/exp6).
room_ledger_period_s_reason: At near_speed_mps=0.3 the robot travels 0.9 m in three seconds, roughly one quarter of the 4 m camera search range. Refresh room boundaries on that motion scale rather than at the 60 Hz command rate.
room_ledger_door_width_m_reason: An assumed upper width for a narrow pedestrian opening, independent of the recorded maps. Cores require more than 0.6 m distance to the edge of sensed free floor. A wider connection retains a core joining the spaces. This is a physical width, not a fitted map or room dimension. Furniture and incomplete sensing can also split floor; labels remain estimates.
room_ledger_covered_share_reason: Release the current room's priority when 90 percent of its sensed indoor floor has camera coverage. A residual 10 percent corresponds to a 0.4 m occlusion strip per 4 m search range. This physical allowance for occlusion is a policy assumption, not a guarantee of person visibility.
room_ledger_dwell_s_reason: Bound time credited to a room by one full scan at scan_yaw_dps=30, 12 s, plus travel over two search radii, 8 m at near_speed_mps=0.3, 26.7 s, rounded to 40 s. This camera and motion budget is independent of seeds and room layouts. It changes frontier priority and never interrupts a safety or person action.
room_auction_reason: Code, not the language model, splits rooms between robots (owner decision, 23 Oct). Each robot radios one room claim: an anchor cell inside the room, the room's radius, its bid in seconds of travel to the room's nearest frontier, when it took the room, and an expiry peer_claim_s after sending. The lowest bid holds the room; a robot that hears a better bid gives its room up. This is the sequential single-item auction of Koenig et al., 'The Power of Sequential Single-Item Auctions for Agent Coordination', AAAI 2006, run without an auctioneer so it works for any number of robots. Needs room_ledger. On since 23 Oct 16:50 with room_ledger (headless exp6).
frontier_turn_cost_reason: A frontier's cost adds the time to turn to its first leg, at limits.max_yaw_rate_dps and expressed in metres at open_speed_mps, when that turn exceeds turn_in_place_deg: beyond it the controller turns on the spot and then walks, so the times add. FUEL (Zhou, Zhang, Gao, Shen, IEEE RA-L 2021, arXiv 2010.11561) scores by max(translation time, yaw time) because a drone yaws while it flies; a legged robot turning in place cannot. The 60 deg/s limit undercharges real turns (measured median 45 deg/s in the headless simulator). Headless seed 5001 (23 Oct): turning in place toward newly chosen goals was 25 to 27 s per robot in 240 s. On since 23 Oct 16:50 with room_ledger (headless exp6).
room_indoor_promotion_reason: Needs room_ledger. A room of the robot's own map whose floor is partly proven indoors (at least frontier_min_information_cells cells) and whose edge is mostly mapped wall (enclosure_min_closed_share, the same share as the walled-in test; edges into other rooms count neither way) is one enclosed space, so all its floor becomes search area and its coverage is measured on all of it. Headless seeds 5001 to 5004 (23 Oct): the LiDAR mapped whole rooms at once, the far side stayed unproven and was never offered as a frontier, and robots left rooms after the near corner. A yard joined to a room by a wide opening has a mostly unknown edge and is not promoted. On since 23 Oct 16:50 with room_ledger (headless exp6).
room_ledger_corridor_first_reason: Needs room_ledger. Corridor frontiers rank before rooms not yet entered, so a robot walks the corridor's length (seeing every door off it) before choosing rooms; finishing the room it stands in still comes first. Doctrine: UK Operational Guidance, Breathing Apparatus, Appendix 5, directional search, 'particularly suitable for domestic' properties; Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, Searching Techniques (2024), threshold search at each doorway (both in codex_briefs/research_23oct/prior_art_23oct.txt). Headless seed 5001 (23 Oct): the kitchen door 17 m down the corridor was never seen from its lower half and the kitchen never entered either robot's ledger. On since 23 Oct 16:50 with room_ledger (headless exp6).
sweep_once_per_room_reason: Needs room_ledger. A robot sweeps (left, right, forward looks) once, on first entering a room of its ledger, instead of at every frontier at least sweep_spacing_m from the last sweep; walking to the room's remaining frontiers covers the rest. Headless seed 5001 (23 Oct): sweeps cost 9 to 15 s of turning and 13 to 19 s of standing per robot in 240 s. On since 23 Oct 17:25 with frontier_local_evidence off (headless exp7, selected on tuning houses 5001-5004).
survivor_squeeze_reason: When no frontier is reachable but unsearched floor in the search area is cut off, and a confirmed person's keep-out is in force, shrink the keep-out's hard core once to survivor_squeeze_core_m so the robot can pass the person. With the full core (0.45 m, including the position error) plus the 0.32 m walking clearance, a person lying in any corridor under about 1.8 m wide seals it; IRC R311.6 allows hallways of 0.914 m. Headless seed 5001 (23 Oct): a person in the hallway sealed it and four rooms beyond went unsearched. Trade-off, stated: the robot then passes closer to a person whose position is uncertain by about 0.2 m (survivor_keepout_core_m reason). On since 23 Oct 16:50 with room_ledger (headless exp6).
survivor_squeeze_core_m_reason: Half an adult's shoulder width, the same anthropometric figure survivor_keepout_core_m starts from, without its position-error allowance.
room_auction_margin_s_reason: One radio broadcast period (scenario radio.broadcast_period_s, 2 s). A bid on the radio can be one period old, and a holder walking at open_speed_mps lowers its own bid by up to one period between messages. A challenger must beat the holder by more than that, otherwise two robots with near-equal bids hand a room back and forth. Within the margin the robot that took the room first keeps it; on equal times the lower robot ID keeps it.
corridor_max_width_m_reason: Widest corridor width any common code requires: 96 in (2438 mm) for Group I-2 corridors where beds are moved, IBC Table 1020.2 (2018 and 2021 editions; read through secondary sources: building code forum and commentary pages, 23 Oct 2026, not the ICC text itself). The narrowest is 36 in for a dwelling hallway, IRC R311.6. A free region wider than 2.44 m is not built as a passage, so it is treated as a room. Width is measured on the robot's own map as twice the largest clearance from free floor to anything not known free.
corridor_min_elongation_reason: A definition, not a measured or sourced value: a corridor is a passage at least three times as long (floor area divided by width) as it is wide. It was chosen before looking at any recorded map and is checked only on synthetic maps in the EditMode tests (a 12 x 1.6 m corridor passes; a 4 x 4 m room with three doors does not). Rooms of the 2:1 proportions found in houses stay rooms.
corridor_min_openings_reason: A definition: a corridor serves several rooms (Shreya's rule, approved 23 Oct: long narrow free regions with several door-width openings). Two openings make a passage through; three or more make a hub that should not be claimed by one robot, because a claim on it would lock partners out of every room off it. An opening is a contact with another room at least one body width (2 x robot_radius_m) wide.
person_rgb_strong_confidence_reason: One colour sighting at this YOLO11m confidence or above makes a person candidate on its own (1.01 = off: two sightings within person_rgb_window_s are needed). Seed 934, robot B: a person on a bed was in the colour view for 1.2 s (21 frames, 0.54 to 0.86, 1.8 m) while the robot turned past; the once-a-second scan caught one frame and the two-sightings rule dropped her until 153 s. Candidates still need the viewing dwell to be confirmed. Headless 24 Oct 01:50 (houses 5001-5004 tuning plus sealed 934, solid bodies, 240 s): with the people, jam, warm-area, blank-wall, fire-cut and meet-up switches on, confirmed 17 -> 19 of 20 against the watchdog-only baseline, 0 false, coverage 78.0 -> 73.3 % (within run-to-run spread on four houses); room_sweep 75.8 %, sealed 934 house 60 -> 63 %. On since 24 Oct 01:55 at 0.7.
person_glance_reason: Any colour sighting at person_glance_min_confidence or above stops the turn and holds the camera on it for person_glance_s, with the colour scan at person_rgb_boost_period_s meanwhile, so repeated scans can make a candidate. Same seed 934 case. person_glance_repeat_s keeps one weak false hit from stopping the robot again and again. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
person_glance_min_confidence_reason: The recorder already asks the vision service for boxes down to 0.25 (RecordingSession PeopleScan min_conf); below the 0.5 candidate level such a box only earns a look.
person_glance_s_reason: Ten scans at the 0.2 s boost period: enough for two sightings in person_rgb_window_s from a robot that is standing.
person_glance_repeat_s_reason: One glance per spot (survivor_merge_m) in this window, so a poster or a warm object that scores 0.3 cannot stop the robot every few seconds.
person_rgb_boost_period_s_reason: Colour scan period while a sighting is live (WantsPeopleBoost); 5 Hz against the usual 1 Hz.
room_ledger_relative_doors_reason: Room cores by hierarchical erosion (Bormann et al., ICRA 2016, Room segmentation): a region becomes two rooms only where rising clearance splits it into two cores of room_ledger_min_core_m2, so a door is any narrowing between wider spaces, not a fixed width; free strips under room_ledger_min_room_m2 are no room. Seed 934: openings of 1.2 to 1.6 m (at or above the fixed 1.2 m door) made foyer, living room and hallway one room, and 126 of robot A's 133 rooms were under 1 m2.
room_ledger_min_core_m2_reason: Smallest core that counts as a room of its own when a region splits: a little more than a body footprint (0.75 x 0.36 m).
room_ledger_min_room_m2_reason: A free strip without a core smaller than this is no room (slivers behind furniture, wall seams).
room_ledger_split_min_m_reason: Lowest clearance threshold: about the robot's half width plus a cell.
room_ledger_split_max_m_reason: Highest clearance threshold tried: a 3 m wide space; wider regions are not split further.
reject_area_memory_reason: A thermal-only warm shape within reject_area_m of a spot rejected (by this robot's agent or a partner's) in the last reject_area_s is not raised again from any side; a colour person sighting still is. Seed 934, robot A in the study: 12 warm patches beside a desk lamp and a globe rejected, each a 10 to 27 s agent step, and they kept coming back from new sides or as new tracks. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
reject_area_m_reason: The blob centres of one heated wall patch moved up to about 1.4 m between rejections in seed 934.
reject_area_s_reason: Half the 240 s mission: long enough not to revisit a known hot wall, short enough that a changed scene is looked at again.
room_sweep_reason: Owner (23 Oct): finish a room from its left side across to the right, as seen from where the robot came in, then leave on the right. Frontiers in the room being finished cost up to room_sweep_s more the further right of the line from the entry point to the room centre they lie. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
room_sweep_s_reason: About one walk across a large room at open speed: the side order wins over small travel differences, not over a far detour.
health_close_surface_reason: A poor colour score with valid depth at or above health_smoke_max_valid_depth is a close featureless surface, not smoke: keep colour mode. Seed 934, robot A: 4 switches to thermal facing blank or heated walls (0 to 7 corners, valid depth 0.80 to 0.99), each slowing the robot and waking an agent step. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
health_smoke_max_valid_depth_reason: Every earlier switch in smoke or haze (30 across 12 recordings) had valid depth 0.50 or less; the 934 wall cases 0.80 or more.
fire_cut_retry_reason: Before declaring no reachable floor, drop this robot's fire-cut exclusions and plan again on the current heat map, at most once per fire_cut_retry_s. Seed 934, robot A: 21 frontiers set aside for the fire margin, then 'no reachable unsearched floor' at 209 s with six house rooms unsearched. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
fire_cut_retry_s_reason: Half the fire_cut_blacklist_s exclusion, so a still-burning route is not retried every planning cycle.
rendezvous_walk_max_s_reason: Cap on the walk back to where the partner was last heard (0 = no cap). Seed 934, robot B walked back 30 s (136 to 166 s) and found nobody. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
pinned_yield_reason: Two robots pinned against each other back up at the same moment into each other. Right of way: the lower id keeps its goal; the other backs straight away (no turn, which would swing into the partner) for pinned_yield_back_s or until pinned_yield_m apart, then steps aside. Headless house 5003 (23 Oct, solid bodies): both robots in contact at the entrance 213 and 217 s of 240. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
pinned_yield_m_reason: Partner closer than this (radio pose) counts as in contact: one body length plus clearance.
pinned_yield_back_s_reason: At pinned_yield_speed_mps, 0.45 m: enough to free a touching body.
pinned_watchdog_reason: A robot that has followed a route for pinned_window_s without its body moving pinned_move_m is pinned, whatever holds it: its goal is set aside for stuck_blacklist_s and it backs up, turns and chooses again. The 3 s holds (the swept-path brake and the safe-chord hold) restart whenever one step passes their check, and the progress watchdog ignores a robot that has not travelled. Headless house 5011 (23 Oct), robot B: 25 s still in a closet doorway with its goal 0.5 m ahead, 65 collision_risk events, 43 s before the goal was set aside. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
pinned_window_s_reason: Longer than any deliberate stop on a route: a 180 deg turn in place takes 3 s at 60 deg/s, and the slow final approach to a goal still moves 0.15 m within a few seconds.
pinned_move_m_reason: Odometry drift and jitter while held stay under about 0.1 m (5011 robot B moved 0.04 m in 25 s); one body step forward is more than this.
candidate_split_reason: A linked partner nearer to a candidate and already heading for it (radio goal within survivor_stop_max_m + 1 m) or standing within the viewing band takes it; this robot leaves it and searches on, and drops one it is already walking to. Headless houses 5003 and 5004 (23 Oct, solid bodies): with one strong sighting enough, both robots raised the same people from the entrance at 0 s, walked up to them together and jammed in the doorway for over 200 s; with the split, contact fell to 1-2 s. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
room_ledger_drop_slivers_reason: Free strips without a room core smaller than room_ledger_min_room_m2 are no room, with the fixed door rule kept. Seed 934: 126 of robot A's 133 ledger rooms were under 1 m2 (median one cell), each with a new id, ranked, claimed and shown to the agent. Separate from room_ledger_relative_doors, which cost house 5001 26 to 34 points of coverage in every headless run. On since 24 Oct 01:55.
candidate_wall_tall_only_reason: The on-wall test for thermal-only candidates counts only occupied cells the camera cannot see over (live 3D map heights), so a bed or sofa is no wall. Seed 934 (23 Oct 20:45), robot B: the kitchen person curled on a bed was flagged 'person-sized depth blob on a long mapped wall' at 14.5, 45.7, 69.9 and 150.4 s, never approached, and confirmed only at 153.5 s by the colour detector. Acts only where the robot has heights (Unity's /map3d layers); headless has none. On since 24 Oct 03:35.
room_walk_in_reason: A real room (room_walk_in_min_m2 or more, not a corridor) searched from its doorway but never entered gets one walk to its own centre cell within room_walk_in_max_m, once per room and once per spot (thrash guard: ledger ids can change). Owner: walk into every room. Headless unseen houses: 17 of 55 rooms never entered. Measured 24 Oct 03:20 (houses 5001-5004 and sealed 934, final config): 0 to 2 walk-ins per run, coverage 73.3 -> 75.8 % mean, confirmed 22 -> 21 of 25. On since 24 Oct 03:35.
step_exact_clearance_reason: The end of one tick's step is judged by its point (robot_radius_m to every obstacle cell's square), not by its cell. Judged by its cell, a 5 mm step stopped the robot on a cell boundary while the chord to its target, sampled every 2.5 cm, passed: it faced a safe chord and could not move. Headless unseen houses (23 Oct final): all 47 safe-chord holds had the body 0.32 to 0.41 m from every wall and furniture edge; house 5021, robot B lost 57 s at a 0.95 m bedroom door in 8 hold, back-up and retry cycles. Fire margins and unknown cells keep the cell rule. OFF until measured.
survivor_view_sight_line_reason: The viewing stop starts only with a mapped line to the candidate clear of walls (GridPlanner.ClearView, which the approach viewpoint already passes) or at the end of the approach path; otherwise the robot keeps walking the approach. Headless house 5022 (23 Oct final), robot A stopped 4.00 m from s1 at 132.5 s with a wall between them and stood until the 40 s approach limit at 168 s; s1 was the one person of 30 never confirmed. OFF until measured.
room_walk_in_min_m2_reason: Smaller spaces are alcoves or furniture gaps, not rooms to walk into.
room_walk_in_max_m_reason: About 13 s at open speed: a detour, not a cross-house trip.
